editorial.marketOverview: The three-session November 23–25 baseline remains bearish with elevated downside risk. Friday's broad technology decline and substantially deeper semiconductor losses show persistent weakness in AI leadership, compounded by elevated implied volatility and weak breadth. Sunday has no US cash equity session; all Friday closing metrics are carried forward as historical observations.
editorial.whatChanged: Sunday reporting reiterates Friday's severe equity liquidation and the Thanksgiving-shortened week's inflation, growth and corporate earnings tests. Secondary weekend reporting of Bitcoin weakness suggests continued speculative risk aversion, but is neither synchronized with Friday equity closes nor proof of Monday Nasdaq selling. Open Watch has no new curated events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The combination of weaker QQQ, sharply underperforming SOX and high VIX suggests forced de-risking rather than an ordinary narrow pullback. A relief bounce is plausible after such losses, but stabilization requires improving breadth, semiconductor relative strength and volatility. The earlier 29-bp 10Y–2Y slope is an unsynchronized indicative calculation and cannot be used as a current curve reading.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: expect unstable price discovery around flash PMIs and chip leadership; distinguish any gap bounce from sustained participation. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Dell/Analog Devices results can test whether hardware demand supports a rebound. Wednesday November 25: PCE/GDP and other releases may dominate rate-sensitive Nasdaq direction ahead of Thanksgiving; actual surprises and market responses remain unknown.
editorial.bullCase: An oversold rebound can extend if QQQ, SOX and SMH recover together, market breadth broadens and VXN/VIX retreat. Better-than-feared PMI, PCE and hardware earnings would provide possible catalysts, but no outcomes are yet known.
editorial.bearCase: Continued semiconductor underperformance, negative breadth and elevated volatility would confirm that the AI leadership unwind is still propagating. Weak macro surprises or hawkish rate repricing could intensify downside, while fresh verified regulatory developments could worsen concentration risk.
